reason: The existing mapping provides a defensible and sufficiently complete regulatory basis. Article 9 establishes the risk management system, which is a continuous process requiring systematic review and updating. Article 72 mandates a post-market monitoring system to collect and analyze data, which feeds into the risk management process. Article 26(5) requires deployers to monitor the system's operation and report issues. Article 20 addresses corrective actions for non-conformity. Together, these provisions cover the monitoring of drift, misuse, control failure, and emerging risks.

challenge_comment: The mapping effectively links the control objective to the core regulatory requirements for risk management and post-market monitoring. The continuous nature of the risk management system (Art. 9) and the systematic data collection (Art. 72) directly support the monitoring of emerging risks. The obligations for deployers (Art. 26(5)) and providers (Art. 20) ensure a comprehensive approach to identifying and addressing issues.
